title: quintuple carries units onto orbit — a machine-checked theorem of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit
description:
quintuple carries units onto orbit — decided over the whole of its finite domain by exhaustion, every case walked by the Lean 4 kernel. Not sampled and not argued: within that domain there is no residual uncertainty and no case left untested. The domain read off the statement is 216 cases — a LOWER BOUND, not a count: where a statement generates its own domain the kernel walks more than the numerals name, and this one is read the same way the paper ranks by it.

Statement (Lean):

[1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8].all (fun d => [1, 2, 4, 8, 7, 5].contains (m9 (5 * d))) ∧ ([1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8].map (fun d => m9 (5 * d))).eraseDups.length = 6

Statement (LaTeX):

\forall d \in [1,\,2,\,4,\,5,\,7,\,8],\; \mathrm{m9}\mathopen{}\left(5 \cdot d\right) \in [1,\,2,\,4,\,8,\,7,\,5] \land \left|\operatorname{dedup}\left(\{\, \mathrm{m9}\mathopen{}\left(5 \cdot d\right) \mid d \in [1,\,2,\,4,\,5,\,7,\,8] \,\}\right)\right| = 6

Proof. by decide — exhausting its domain, of which the statement names 216 cases. Checked sorry-free; #print axioms reports no axiom dependency. No Mathlib, no native_decide. □

What this record establishes. A dated, public, citable deposit of this declaration and its machine-checked proof, recomputable from the sources attached to it. That is priority, and the record proves it on its own. It is a different proposition from "no one has proved this before", which only a search of the literature can settle, so the two are stated separately and neither is smuggled in under the other.

Novelty: UNCLASSIFIED — an open question, not a claim. No prior-art search has been performed for this source file, so this record asserts priority of deposit and nothing about the literature.

Verification. The proof needs 2 files, all attached: src/proof/imagined.lean, src/proof/z9.lean. Check it with lake env lean src/proof/imagined.lean src/proof/z9.lean, or clone https://github.com/ceccec/millennium-solutions and run npm run lean. The content-address of this declaration is recorded as lean_imagined_quintuple_carries_units_onto_orbit at https://ceccec.github.io/millennium-solutions/theorem/lean_imagined_quintuple_carries_units_onto_orbit. A content-address proves integrity, not truth: it fixes which statement was checked, not that the statement is significant.

Scope, stated as plainly as the claim. The declaration is decided over a finite domain. It settles no Clay Millennium Problem, asserts no quantum speedup, and describes no physical system. 0/7.
